speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here for acute diarrhea; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me how many times you have had loose stools in the last 24 hours?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI).

The patient is an 58-year-old female on levofloxacin who developed acute, frequent watery diarrhea with cramping; this clinical picture strongly suggests antibiotic-associated colitis caused by C. difficile. Given the high suspicion, I will request stool testing for C. difficile toxins or PCR. REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_difficile_toxin_and_PCR
